I will have to clarify all of that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You have the full right to cross-examine this witness on all those matters, but before you pose a question, you better set a time frame at the beginning of your question so that all of us could know where you are heading for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. You have to know that there are two constitutions of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm sorry that I always have to give these explanations with witnesses listening to my explanations. I wanted to come to this through my questions. There was a constitution, there was a socialist constitution, and then there was another constitution that was drafted, but that was never accepted because it was never adopted by all three peoples, and until the present day there is still no constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina in this form of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina as exists today. The state of Bosnia-Herzegovina does not exist even today, because it consists of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Srpska. It is an union of two states within one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, your job is to do the cross-examination. I hope that what you said is the answer from this witness, rather than your statement. You may proceed with your cross-examination. Just remember that you have to put your question in a concise and precise way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now that we have mentioned this constitutional decision, tell me, in order for a decision to become legal, both a decision made by a government and of the constitutional court, do the representatives of all three peoples have to be present when such a decision is being made?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina adopted a constitution --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I do apologise for interrupting you. But please, would you be so kind as to answer. It was very brief.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are talking about the law now. I think this is really going to tire us out and a lot of time would be needed to explain all of this. It would be time consuming, wouldn't it? But in principle, yes, of course, under normal circumstances, that's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know which judges adopted this decision, who signed on it, who were on the Supreme Court in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that the government and war presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina was a legal war presidency elected by all three constituent peoples? Do you know or not know, if you can just follow my questions?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I can follow you. Of course I can. However, we are going in a direction of law and constitution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Let me rephrase the question. Was there rotation in the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina as provided by the constitution adopted by the will of all three peoples after the first democratic elections? In other words, was there a different president or presidency from a different ethnic group every year?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In late -- sorry, in the beginning of 1993, on the basis of this principle of rotation, was Mr. Izetbegovic supposed to turn over the presidency to another member?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The obstructions had already started in order to break up Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time, so there was no one to turn the presidency to at that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but you did not quite answer my question. Did he or did he not turn over his post to someone else?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was that the reason why representatives of the Serbian and Croatian ethnic groups left the government and the institutions of presidency?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what the name of the Croatian member of the presidency was?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a period of time, that was Mr. Komsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know in 1993, that is, the period that we are dealing with, who it was?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a period of time, it was -- I would need to remember this. I would need to recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a period of time, it was Mr. Boras. And then after him, they changed; I think Lasic and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Boras was elected in the democratic elections which were conducted, and it was through the elections that he became a member of the presidency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know when he left the presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. This is what I needed to hear. In the presidency in other political bodies, could the members of these bodies only be those who were elected through the democratic process?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how it should have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was Alija Izetbegovic not the president between 1993 and 1996 -- -9 almost?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So then, was he a legal president?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Regardless of the fact that he did not abide by the constitution, the laws, and the will of people which provided that the presidents would rotate every year?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Counsellor, it was a state of war. You see, what changes took place and how the policy changed -- the Croatian people elected Kljujic in a legal manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me. I was asking you about Mr. Alija Izetbegovic. We will come to Mr. Kljujic later. His refusal to turn over the presidency did not lead to a conflict and the abandonment of all institutional posts by the Croats and Serbs and only the Muslims remained?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The real reasons were the agreements between presidents Tudjman and Milosevic and their satellites in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a little bit. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you attend a meeting between Mr. Tudjman and Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know what was discussed there?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public was informed by the public figures of Croatia who knew about what went on there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was this information speculation on the part of journalists, and is this what is the basis of your information?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was from what Mr. Stjepan Mesic, president of Croatia, stated and other officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Stjepan Mesic was not in Karadzordzevo and stated that publicly. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, you were shown a document, unsigned, no stamp, talking about some guarantees. This was in Graz at some alleged meeting between the representatives of the Serb and Croat groups?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was the basis of your knowledge of that also speculation in newspapers?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One learns about everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, was there a "media war," if I can put it in quotation marks, between the Muslim media, electronic and print, as well as the Croat and Serb ones?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there were inflammatory pieces and propaganda in the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna and obviously in the Republika Srpska and in the Serbian media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How about the Muslim media?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was only by exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, you as a religious leader, did you not go on Radio Mostar and announced the -- Mr. Ismet Hadziosmanovic, did you not personally declare that he was sacked on Radio Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please tell this Trial Chamber, what does the Mufti of Mostar have to do with politics, let alone to announce the removal of a political official?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need some time to explain that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you give me some time, I will do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We will come to that point, but I want to continue with my questions. Can you tell me, can you link the religious activities and politics?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would that not be analogous to Bishop Peric's announcing on radio that, for instance, Mate Boban was removed from power?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be similar. But Bishop Peric had no reason for it, but I did have a reason. And that was not my own will. That was the will of the Bosniak people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you confirm for me the contention that among the Muslims in Herzegovina, there were those who were -- the locals who were there -- who were indigenous and who always wanted to negotiate with Croats, but there were those who had come as refugees and who had contributed to the rising of tension and who did not want to negotiate?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That does not reflect the real situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: It does not reflect the real situation. Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In other words, all Muslims were for dialogue and for tolerance, both the locals and the newcomers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Why, then, was Mr. Hadziosmanovic removed from his post?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosniak people removed him because he did not represent the interests of Bosniaks in a right way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Sir, did you not establish and lead the Council of Muslims of Herzegovina as a parallel institution of the SDA at the instruction of Mr. Izetbegovic in order to remove Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, sorry, Mr. Hadziosmanovic, but at the instructions of Mr. Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to organise within the Muslim community forces which through legal means and through a democratic process would decide on the removal of Mr. Hadziosmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please take the bundle provided to you by the Prosecution? And I think this is the Exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I could be wrong. I've been trying to listen along in the French, and I noticed that the English transcript the question was whether, on line 16, the witness did something in order to remove Mr. Izetbegovic, and I don't know whether that should be, in fact, a reference to the removal of Mr. Hadziosmanovic, but I see that it has been corrected. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have a good point, but this witness is not yours, so you are not allowed to make any interventions at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott. Well, Mr. Krsnik, would you please clear it up for us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. And I appreciate the comment of -- again, this is part of the fact that we speak the same language and sometimes it's difficult to follow us. The question was clear, whether it was at instructions of Mr. Izetbegovic, who at the time was legal president of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Witness -- the witness established the Council of Muslims of Herzegovina as a parallel force against Mr. Hadziosmanovic and through which organisation he was removed, and eventually they succeeded in doing so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is this correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, Mr. Hadziosmanovic had Mr. Izetbegovic's support. We wanted to express the will of Bosniaks, and we wanted this to reach Mr. Izetbegovic so that he could direct Mr. Hadziosmanovic to resign.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind and open the bundle to the page where the Exhibit P173.1 is? Look -- please look at the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot find it. What page is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Actually, it's not a page. Actually, 626 at the top, right corner but the exhibit is P173.1. The last three digits in the top, right corner should be 626.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I believe this is paragraph 2 of the alleged letter by Mr. Hadziosmanovic to the Croatian Party of Democratic -- to the Croatian Democratic Union, to the president personally. First off, do you know Mr. Hadziosmanovic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was it customary for him not to sign letters that he wrote?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found this in a computer, so we do not have all the documents. I had a number of documents with signatures affixed, but as I said, my archives were seized in western Mostar, but we were able to save this in the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, who is "we"? You said "we." What computer was this and when did you find it?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was saved in our -- by our technical department.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, where was this computer?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the team that worked with me. There were people who saved this -- the certain documents that we wrote, and our technical service saved it on a diskette.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the team that worked with you, what did this team work on?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It worked on this document that you're referring to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you confirm to me that it was you and your team who found this document and then provided it to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: This document you found, you had a team that worked on this?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. At a time when the -- when the document was drafted, we had a team, but this is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. This is your document. Were you a member of the Party of Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you ever attend any meetings, gatherings of this party?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you ever with the military? Did you take an active part with the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not bear arms, I did not wear a uniform, but I did cooperate with them, and I can say that I cooperated actively on the moral support; that is, I was with people in the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you go to their ceremonies?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Again to provide moral support?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the only legal armed force of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You see, I have my questions, but as you give me your answers, I have to ask you different questions.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The HVO was also a legal force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, until it became a renegade force and an aggressor against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you understand the concept of aggressor?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: An aggressor has to come from outside, otherwise it's civil war.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was supported from outside by Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. Very well. Let me take you to paragraph 2 of this unsigned letter which you found somewhere in your computer. And the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The issue should be squarely put to this witness, if it, in fact, is Mr. Krsnik's position. If he's putting to the witness that this letter is falsified, and this letter was not in fact put -- prepared by Dr. Hadziosmanovic, then I think he should put that squarely to this witness and give the witness a chance to respond, if that's in fact his position, if he truly is contending that that's not a letter from Dr. Hadziosmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that is not my contention. It is a very simple question. I just asked the witness about it. He explained what it is. I asked why it was not signed, and he explained why. I see nothing unusual about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are not challenging the authenticity of this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For now, I don't. If I am allowed to ask questions, I think that it is all going to be very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President, but I don't know what "for now" means. Does he challenge the authenticity of the letter or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let me ask the witness to -- let me read this, and then we will be very clear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is impossible for the interpreters to follow the speed of this reading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to remind both of you, since you are speaking the same language, so please do make a pause after each question or answer. Witness, you might not be familiar with the proceedings in this Tribunal. In front of you, you have a screen. Every word will be translated and appear in that screen. When you see the sentence is finished, you may begin to answer the question. Otherwise, we cannot follow up with both of you. Also, whatever you say has to be translated from English to French, which makes it more difficult for those French listeners to catch up with you. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I think this is the paragraph I was reading: "Many signs of the Croatian and Muslim people have given their lives to the freedom -- for freedom in the course of the common war in the territory of Mostar and Herzegovina, which is why we must engage in a democratic dialogue to create the conditions for regaining the mutual trust that has been undermined. To this end, we would like to draw attention to all the good that the Republic of Croatia has done for the Muslims from Bosnia and Herzegovina." The letter was written, I believe, on 14 September 1992. And in a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. democratic dialogue, Mr. Hadziosmanovic lists the items that needs to be addressed. Is that not a democratic way of addressing things?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you removed from office such a person?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Read the next line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of course. And I will agree that it should be tendered into evidence, because it shows the capacity for democracy of this man. Of course, there were misunderstandings that needed to be resolved on the 14th of September, 1992. Of course, they were political parties, is that correct, with different political programmes? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So then political parties meet, and they talk, discuss things; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And if I look at this letter, I believe that Mr. Hadziosmanovic was the right person to do this. You don't think so?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, what's the relevance of this question? Is there any dispute that Mr. Hadziosmanovic wrote this letter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we would like to hear the answer from this witness. Yes, if you have an answer, Witness, you may answer this question.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Hadziosmanovic, in these 10 or 12 items that he wrote, confirmed all the objections that we listed in the documents that we had produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is your view of things. Is this your view of this document, the way you just said? This is your point of view, this is your standpoint? This is how you read this letter?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how I read it, and that's how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Did Mr. Hadziosmanovic come from one of the oldest families in Mostar, who has lived there for generations, for centuries?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one of the most reputed Mostar families. I don't know how many centuries they lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you deny that a person of that kind would be the best suited to know the political climate and the mentality of people in the area? Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unless -- and this is hard for me to say because I would like to keep his authority intact. But in a way, he must not betray his own people, because in every people, you have someone who -- *** [Cannot distinguish between Q and A] ***

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. A person who is seeking democratic dialogue, cooperation, common life with another ethnic group in the same area and who is trying to work on solving these problems. And as he said in a meeting -- and I'm going to quote -- excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, while he's looking for that, the transcript, as you probably know, has got the answers and questions all mixed up. So it's hard to -- just note that for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krsnik, could you tell us which document are you using right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are my own notes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think we have made a rule that we have to be informed beforehand. And also in fairness to this witness, you could not just fish a document and read something. That's not fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not intend to use this document at all. These are simply my notes, and I have thousands of those. I just wanted to remember the date. You will hear the question. It will all be quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you present at a meeting --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just say something? This document, the way it is now, even though it was signed by Hadziosmanovic, I accept that 100 percent. So let's get this over with, because it is along the lines of the interests of the Croats and the Bosniaks. So let's just cut it short.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you at the meeting of the regional committee of the SDA on the 10th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The 10th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: May I remind you that there was a big quarrel at that meeting between Safet Orucevic and his group and Hadziosmanovic and his group?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you perhaps informed about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were you present at a meeting on the 16th of April, 1993, the meeting was attended by the representatives of the army of the 4th Corps, the representatives of the Council of Bosniaks of Herzegovina, you and Efendi Tinjak --

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: -- when all Muslims were requested to leave schools, political councils, and all organisations in the HZ HB. Hadziosmanovic opposed it, then saying that he wants misunderstandings to be resolved by dialogue, not in blood. After that Mitar Hujdur, the late Mitar Hujdur, said that he would take the town of Mostar with his boys within one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I truly am, but that's not the proper way to put a question. You can start by saying, "Were you at a meeting?" If the witness says no, he was not at the meeting, it's improper to then suggest all these things happened at a meeting which this witness doesn't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you. Mr. Krsnik, this witness said very clear that he was not at the meeting. And how could you cross-examine on the contents of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, these are two different meetings, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the date of that meeting, if I may know?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 16th of April. I asked him very simply, and I explained who was present. Just a minute, my learned friend. The point of this cross-examination is to get answers that we shall then either disprove or deny with our own witness.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, before you informed me the meeting was on the 16th of April, we all were on the meeting of the 10th of April, 1993. I think there's a misunderstanding between us and between you and your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues who are following the transcript say that it's all there in the transcript very nicely. At any rate, there is a misunderstanding, so I'll try to slow down with my questions, because they tell me that the relevant date was there. In the meantime, I did get an answer from the witness to my question, and that was he said that he did not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And my final question with regard to this meeting: At the meeting of the Islamic community on the 29th of April, 1993, you were present, as well as Efendi Kojic, Efendi Tinjak, and Mr. Zijo Demirovic, president of the regional committee by then, if I'm not mistaken. You established there, and you passed a kind of decision stating that it is only the policy of Alija Izetbegovic that can be abided by, and Mr. Zijo Demirovic stated that Mostar has to be an Islamic city in all its glory. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Honourable witness, tell me, please, imams, hodzas, were they war commanders and commanders in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and did they actively participate in the war?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you give me some from your own Mufti territory?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halilovic, Nezim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is that the commander of the 4th Light Cavalry Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Where is he now?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is now in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot tender this now. I just received it. So I'll try to have it photocopied during the break. Namely, the newspapers carried a story stating that the mentioned gentleman went on a trip and is now in Afghanistan. I'm asking you now whether you know this because he belongs to your Mufti territory?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, newspapers write about all sorts of things, and you just received this and this is the first that I've ever heard of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to the relevance of something that happened in 2001, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Mr. Krsnik, we are not to go into this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw this question. I withdraw this question. But, Your Honour, I shall have many questions for this witness, because it is only through this witness that the Honourable Trial Chamber can understand the nature of certain things that were going on in Bosnia-Herzegovina. So this question of mine was not put just like that, because I know what is relevant and what is irrelevant. Nevertheless, I withdraw it. You will see later, through my further examination, why I put this particular question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have full right to do your cross-examination, but just within certain limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do beg your pardon, Your Honour. Of course, I am not going to engage in dialogue with you, ever. I shall simply abide by your rulings. When the Prosecutor asked witnesses about certain persons, he would end by putting a question, by saying, "Where is this person now?" And then these questions were allowed. And that is particularly what he asked Mr. Van Hecke. So that's why I thought that I could ask this witness where the mentioned gentleman is nowadays. I'm going to give you the exact question that the Prosecutor put to Mr. Van Hecke, was, "Where is Ivan Andabak now?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is that we have not seen that piece of newspaper. You could not get something from your pocket and show him and ask whether you know this person is in a certain place in the world. So I've already reminded you that before your cross-examination, you have to photocopy all those documents and furnish them to everybody. I think only by doing so it is fair to everyone. You may proceed, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to tell the Trial Chamber what an emir is and what is the position that an emir holds in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a position which was sometimes official and sometimes voluntary in the units that had an Islamic background.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that some units of the BH army had an Islamic background and others did not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. And tell me, the 4th Corps, did it have an Islamic background or not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were units that wanted, in their own special way, to regulate their private, personal lives. This was a smaller group of persons who wanted to carry out Muslim rituals, to have Muslim food, and to behave within the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a separate unit, whereas others, the rest, were free men, so to speak; that is to say, that they could come from Muslim background but they did not necessarily have to, on the other hand. However, these were a group of persons who, through their personal and family lives, wanted to establish a special code of conduct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the 4th Corps have an emir of its own?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning, at the beginning, there was one, until the separate unit was founded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, after the 9th of May - we are relying on this date because that's what the indictment says, 1993, 1994, and 1995 - can you give me a single Croat or a Serb's name that was in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Were there ten of them or were there 100 of them or a thousand?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a personnel officer of the army, and I didn't count them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, how can Islam go along with an army which was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. created on a democratic basis of a democratic state and it expresses the obligation and duty of all the citizens of that particular state?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: For example, when the army has a salute and when they salute the homeland, for example, do they also have a salute saying Allah-u-ekber?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not an adequate salute from our point of view. It is used -- Allah-u-ekber is used for different things, not as a salute in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I am moving slowly because your salute, your form of greeting, is al salam ou alaykum. I'm going through all of this for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when I said "Allah-u-ekber," was that the salute that could be heard when there were lineups, military reviews, and when men went into fighting? Is that a call that was heard, to Allah?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly in some units, yes, smaller units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, honourable witness, is this acceptable for Croats and Serbs in a common army?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, then, tell me, how come the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina has the exclusive right to say that they are the only army that is liberating Bosnia and Herzegovina and that state belongs to three peoples?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it is pervading political opinion that prevailed and turned their own military units against the interests of the internationally recognised state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina ever have been internationally recognised had the Croats not voted in the referendum for its independence?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it would not have. No, it wouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Honourable witness, a lot of reference has been made to language. You're a learned man. The Bosnian language -- first of all, in order for a language to be a language, doesn't it have to have grammar and spelling rules?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The Bosnian language, did it have its grammar and spelling rules and everything else that would make a language a language in 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, or 1995?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did, since 1903. The beginning of the 20th century, to be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Did you go to school in Bosnia-Herzegovina? I mean primary school, secondary school, university.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What's the language that you studied and what are the languages that existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially and legally, there were the Bosnian and the Croat languages that were recognised. No, sorry, Serbian and Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You studied in Bosnia-Herzegovina in a language which was called Serbo-Croat or Croato-Serb only; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbo-Croat or Croato-Serb, it boils down to the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But I mean the official terminology was precisely that, wasn't it? And one week the Roman script was used in schools for writing and then the next week the students would write in the Cyrillic script; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not exactly, but, yes, yes. People knew both scripts, both alphabets, and if necessary, they wrote both Cyrillic and Latin. Excuse me, we cannot just forget about this. I have to tell you why we did not study the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Don't worry. I'm going to put the right questions to you. I'm going to put that question to you straight away so we're going to resolve this: The Bosnian language, it was not constitutional, legal, and as such, it did not exist from 1945 until 1997, not in a single constitution. It did not exist according to any one of these constitutions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not quite correct. It did exist, but it was not recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And when was the Bosnian language officially established; do you know that? In which year?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you know full well -- I mean, Your Honours, I have to say this. There was a certain discrimination in the former system against Bosniaks, both from the side of greater Serbian ambitions and greater Croatian ambitions. So Muslims from a national ethnic point of view were disenfranchised. Therefore, non-recognition of the Bosnian language in documents is not a denial of the language itself. We spoke that language, as we do speak it today. However, there were tendencies for the Bosniak people, as they are called nowadays, to become assimilated, either to become part of the Croatian people or of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik. The other day, we have already come across the issue of language with another witness. We have got the picture of how the languages are used in that area. It seems to me that the issue of language will get us nowhere. Would you please finish this set of the questions concerning the language as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. I shall abide by every one of your rulings.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, what are the national groups, the ethnic groups, that existed in Bosnia-Herzegovina until 1974?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosniak nation was not there. That's what you're asking me, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the first time I have a witness who is a learned man and with whom I can paint the right kind of picture for the Honourable Trial Chamber. So you're the first person who has given me an answer to this question. I thank you for that. Now, would you please explain to the Trial Chamber the meaning of the word "Muslim"? What does "Muslim" mean in Arabic? I'll tell you why. Sometimes people say that they are Muslim. Sometimes they say they are Bosniak. Some people want me to call them Bosnians. Let's just clarify this terminology. I think that you are the only person who can really clarify the matter for us.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Muslim" means a man devoted to God.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So Islam is a faith?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Islam is a faith.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is it, then, right to say that you are a Bosniak of the Islamic faith?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is right to say from an ethnic point of view that we are Bosniaks, without this adjective "of Islamic faith."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So what is right? What do you say about members of the Islamic faith who live in Croatia or in Germany? Is it right to say that this is a Croat of Islamic faith, for example?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With our national minority in Zagreb, in Croatia, we have a problem. We have a problem because they have not become part of the constitution. They are not recognised as the Bosniak ethnic group, the Bosniak national group. They are called "Croats of the Islamic faith."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind as to tell this Honourable Trial Chamber -- actually, I think it's easiest to proceed in the following way: Muslims participated -- and you're the one who mentioned Pavelic. Didn't Muslims participate in Ustasha establishments, in Ustasha authorities and units by 80 percent?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A large number of them were in the home guards, the home guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that was not -- Ustasha --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it's only pertinent that Ustasha be given some definition, because I don't think in the proceedings so far there has been any explanation of that. If it's a term that Mr. Krsnik is going to use, it should be expressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We believe that this Chamber has made a ruling that we do not use all those terms like "Ustasha." Can you paraphrase these terms in other ways, other terms, rather than use this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By all means, Your Honour. I wanted to clarify that situation, as well, although my learned friend is impatient. I wanted to clarify this for your benefit because my client has been accused of forcing others to sing Ustasha songs, so we are interested in that. Why would an Ustasha song offend Muslims? Because it is a historical fact. And now I see the extent to which I will have to go into this matter in my case, because the Muslims -- I will have to bring bundles of books. Muslims had a common state with the Croats. At that time, they were Croats of the Islamic faith, and that is what I was getting at, but I'm not being allowed to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, if a witness said certain words, I think it's excusable because they are not familiar with the rules of this Trial Chamber. Please, we do not allow those words uttered by Defence counsel. Do you understand the difference? Since we are almost approaching 1.00, we will resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.58 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you to answer the following question: Regarding the Geneva negotiations and the signing of the Vance-Owen Plan, took place in January of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is. I don't necessarily know, but I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, was it only the Serbs who refused to sign this peace accord?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know that on the basis of the Vance-Owen Plan, Bosnia is divided into provinces, and where the majority of the population of a province is Bosnian, all authority was to be in the hands of the Bosnian population; in those provinces where the majority population was Serbian, the authority would be Serbian; and where the Croats were in the majority, they would have the power?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question, Your Honour, as not stating the facts. It's an improper characterisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, would you please rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: On the basis of the Vance-Owen Plan, was the Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina -- actually, did the Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina issue an order where in areas with the majority Bosniak population, the Croats would be placed under the command of the ABiH, and where the Croats were in the majority, the Bosniaks would place themselves under the command of the HVO? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, I truly am sorry, Mr. President, but these are very important matters. Is he talking about military matters or the entire civil political government? Or what's the nature of the question? Because I suggest to the Chamber it's a completely different answer based on the way the question is put.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe it's about the military structures rather than civilian ones. Maybe the witness could clear it up when he is answering this question.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was one in a series of agreements and signed documents which were not implemented and which were not binding. In fact, we can say that these were proposed solutions rather than solutions themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does a signature on an international agreement in which all of the European community took part and on the basis of which the Vance-Owen Plan and peace were achieved appear not binding?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not want to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please look at the P214? This is the exhibit in the blue binder that you received. Can you please find the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I am a bit lost here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you find it, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'll read it very slowly. "On the basis of the agreement, in line with the agreements which were reached and signed at the International Conference on the Former Yugoslavia and the Peace Agreement in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and then in parentheses it says (Geneva Agreements), the HVO of the HZ HB reached a decision at a special meeting in Mostar on 15 January 1993. The following decision: All units of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina currently deployed in the Regions 3, 8, and 10, which were proclaimed Croatian in the Geneva Agreements, shall be subordinated to the command of the main headquarters of the HVO armed forces. "All units of the HVO armed forces that are currently deployed in the Areas 1, 5, and 9, which were proclaimed Muslim in the Geneva Agreements, shall be subordinated to the command of the General Staff of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina command." And then Item 4: "This decision is considered provisional and shall remain in force until the Geneva agreement on the organisation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina is finally signed." And Item 6: "This decision shall be implemented by the head of the Defence Department of the HVO of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna." Do you know that this decision was issued based on the Vance-Owen Plan, the Geneva Agreements, which from -- which in turn flowed this order of the head of the Defence Department of the HVO which was then, in turn, to be implemented, in this case, HZ HB, and in the case of Muslims, the General Staff of the AbiH, that is the BH side. Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you now please look at Exhibit Number 215 of the Prosecutor, and this would be the next one.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a comment on this --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness, you need to answer my next question.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I'll have to come back to it at some point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, we will go back to it if necessary. Will you please open the next exhibit in the sequence; that is, Exhibit P215, please. You have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, based on the decision of the HVO, of the HZ HB, this was back in item 6 of the other document, Bruno Stojic, who was the head of the department at the time, brought -- issued an order which was identical order to the one which we had looked at a moment ago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And the alleged ultimatum was published in a newspaper. We only know that the name of the newspaper is "Borba," and it's also there in your clutch of documents, and that's all. And on the basis of this newspaper article, you concluded that these orders and these decisions were actually ultimatums?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on the basis of a newspaper article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you did it on the basis of these decisions and orders?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These decisions were considered provisional, and we considered them provisional, as is stated here, not final. However, the Croatian side --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, let me lead you by questions, with your permission. I'm in the role of asking questions. It's just simply my position, so please be so kind to ask you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you have to allow this witness to finish his answering. He did not finish his answering of the question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to voice my objection or complaint because some questions really require explanations. They are not -- they cannot be answered with a simple yes or no. The Chamber will not be able to gain a full understanding if I were to answer some questions with just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I will take into consideration your objection, and let me ask you the following question, sir: On the basis of binding -- of binding international agreements, as was the one in Geneva --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is improper. All that's been put in front of the witness are two documents by the HVO. This is the HVO interpretation. Now, if Mr. Krsnik has signed international documents recognition treaties, signed by all the parties, then I suggest he may put those in front of the witness and ask him questions. I don't think, frankly, Mr. Krsnik is getting the answers he thinks he's getting because only a few minutes ago, for instance, after a long statement about this document, he asked the witness, "Do you know about it?" The witness said yes. He didn't say he agreed with it. He said, "I know, I know about the document." I don't think the Chamber is being assisted, Your Honour, by looking at one-sided documents. So I object to having a question put to the witness which mischaracterises the facts. Have the international agreement that the parties signed, if there is one, put in front of the witness and give him a chance to explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Defence counsel has the right to ask the document from one side, but we have to allow this witness to do some explanations on this issue. For instance, as the previous question, the witness has not finished his answer. We haven't received that answer. We gave this witness another chance, but you asked another question, Mr. Krsnik. That's not fair. The witness says that this agreement was regarded as temporary and the Croatian side -- then you stopped him. Let him answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you see that I ask questions and take answers with full respect, but allow me to respond to the comments of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. We have made rulings already on this issue. We don't want you to engage in the argument between the two sides. We will give more opportunity to the witness for him to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me, if you will allow me, I will move on. Yesterday, if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think the Court just ruled that the witness should be allowed to answer a question about five minutes back, and it's gone off my screen so I can't see it, but I think the Court ruled that he should be allowed to finish his response. I don't know how to make the screen go back; otherwise, I'd do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not standing to object.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I -- may I give an explanation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. You just told us you regarded this as temporary agreement, and then you said that the Croatian side -- then you were stopped. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian side considered that agreement the final one. That means they prejudiced the solution. Something that was in the form of a proposal, they took things that they wanted, that on the basis of our experience, of the Bosniak side, with the HVO, with the Croatian component, which never behaved in an open and sincere manner, we could not allow that our -- we could not allow ourselves to turn over our defence to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. You may continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, my first question was whether these decisions were adopted pursuant to orders and internationally signed agreements of the Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. If you recall, that was my initial question.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who was the Minister of Defence at that time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: The Minister of Defence in the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time -- in which at that time all three ethnic groups participated, and on the basis of agreement of the three parties, Mr. Bozo Rajic was appointed Minister of Defence?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very important that we should know this, and that is why I asked. Because Bozo Rajic in all his public utterances was spokesperson for the HVO, and he was a minister who never took office and never went to Sarajevo but, instead, only served interests of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, this was not his personal decision but, rather, the decision of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. On the basis of that decision, a person who is a minister of a certain department was to write such an order; do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bozo Rajic was appointed to the post of Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina but never took over the post.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Witness, you said that you and the ABiH always fought for a unified and indivisible Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm going to offer a document. I would like to ask the registrar -- sorry, the usher to distribute this document. It is only in Croatian language. The document is being translated, but it is not finished, so I will ask for the assistance of interpreters. Can we have it marked temporarily as D1/24.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, would you please turn to page 2 of the document and tell me whether that is your signature.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Is this a letter that you, Mr. Zijad Demirovic, and Faruk Cupina [phoen] sent to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and it is entitled "A warning from Mostar"?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please turn to page 2, now, second paragraph, sixth sentence. Will you please read that full sentence or anything else, but I would like to especially point out that sentence: "In these conditions, the imperative is ..." and so on. That's the beginning of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody was adding things here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In this sentence, nobody added anything.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This may be a proposed solution of some issues that were a topic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please read the sentence.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you, again, tell me which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Then I'll read it. "In such conditions, the imperative is that a division of Bosnia into three ethnically based provinces, with the Muslim province in the Neretva River valley ..." Is this the text? In other words, you advocated division?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, because that is not the spirit of this letter. We said if it is inevitable, if the division is into ethnically -- along ethnic lines inevitable, then the Bosniaks would agree to nothing but this, should it happen. And we were never advocating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Let me read the penultimate paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object to this procedure. The Chamber has now ruled, since the first week of trial, on a set of procedures to be followed with documents. The Prosecution has worked very hard to try to comply with the Court's rulings. One of the requirements, I believe, is that any exhibit be placed -- be interpreted into at least English or French. We are completely unable to follow this evidence, the cross-examination. I don't know to what extent other sentences or phrases are omitted. I cannot follow at all what's happening without having been provided the documents, as this Chamber has ordered, now several times, including, again, just recently the other day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, could I know the sources of this document, where did you get this document? Are there any translations of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President and Your Honours, the gentleman himself verified the authenticity of this document. He signed it, and this is why I proceeded. I received this document through my investigators. They will in due course confirm its authenticity. Nothing was omitted and nothing was added except for a remark of my legal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. assistant. As you can see, it is handwritten, and it is a comment, a note. And I will read it to you. And it is just something that was done in the process of our work. And with the interpreter's help, let me read it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, this Trial Chamber will certainly not accept this document with a note put by your investigators, and not alone. There is no English translation for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will actually file a motion today asking for a Status Conference to discuss various matters. The Defence is making superhuman efforts to abide by your ruling on continuation of this case in chief. We simply were unable to finish the translation. I think we have about 1.000 documents - and I'm just giving you a rough estimate of 1.000 documents - which are in the process of being translated. But these are two very short excerpts. The document is signed. We believe that the letter is very important because, in later stages, you will come to realise how important this document is. And I can read this note or remark to you. It also will be translated into English. So if -- with your permission, I will just finish reading this excerpt and the handwritten note and then I will finish with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, as an exception, I could allow you to read certain paragraphs and those handwritten, but as a rule -- but as a rule, we could not accept this document as evidence as it is. At least you have to provide us with a clean copy, with the translations into the other language. This is the rule we made. Of course, you have full right to make a motion concerning any conferences, especially the Status Conference. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So I'm reading the penultimate section: "If the only way out for us as human beings, and as neighbours, is the continuation of war with all new sacrifices and consequences and victims, we shall do our best to fully mobilise Muslims in this area as early as possible." Above the words, "we are ready," there is an arrow and a note: "They did not conduct mobilisation against the Chetniks." That's the note. My question is: On the 5th of January, 1993, against who were you prepared to mobilise all the Muslims in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document has to be understood in the following way, addressed to Mr. Izetbegovic in his negotiating position. If - if - there is a territorial division, he would have our support, and that he should simply take into consideration our requests. I would like to remind the Trial Chamber, with their permission, that it would be a good thing to read the paragraph from the beginning, not only the second part of the paragraph, and you have deliberately avoided that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, you know, this is the very problem of this issue, that you cannot read a paragraph out of context. So that's why this Trial Chamber made a ruling that you have to submit this document with its translation so that at least we could see the whole picture of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am giving the entire letter. I am going to tender it in its entirety. I gave it to the witness in his own language, and only in order to save time, I've read two sections. If I were to read out the whole thing, I think I'd take up too much time. I am going to tender the entire letter.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allow me, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, before this Trial Chamber, the fairness should prevail over the efficiency. We have to be fair to the witness, to the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm certainly trying to be that. Had I not presented this document today, I think I would have acted against the interests of the witness and the Defence, and I thought it was far more important to present this in the witness's language, and it's the language he understands. It was more important, I think, than only the translation, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, can you skip this document for the later stage? Because we cannot judge just out of certain paragraphs from this document. But I could promise you that we'll receive this document with the translations, then we'll consider whether to admit it into evidence or not at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, are you familiar with the programme of the SDA party?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, superficially. I wouldn't have to be familiar with it, with that programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness: Are you familiar with the "Islamic Declaration"?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I was not a member of any party, the SDA included. That is in response to your first question. I am aware of the "Islamic Declaration," the book that Mr. Alija Izetbegovic wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that because of that book, the "Islamic Declaration," Mr. Izetbegovic was sentenced to many years in prison because of the -- his extremist views?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the fact that Mr. Izetbegovic was convicted, not because of his extremist views but because of the prohibition of freedom of thought in the communist regime, freedom of expression and writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was informed today from the Registry that they will not have it translated for me because I had given it to them to have it translated for this person. They told me that it was already translated for the OTP. And I am going to present some positions from the "Islamic Declaration." Perhaps I'll do that at a later stage, but I would like to ask them for translation of the "Islamic Declaration," of course, unless the gentlemen from the OTP have the "Islamic Declaration" translated here with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, in direct contrast to what we have witnessed over the past 20 minutes, the translation is here. It has been provided. I'm happy to provide it to counsel. And here it is, through the usher. I think English translations could be provided to us of Defence documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, I find this very strange, because all those documents you use in your cross-examination, you ask the other side to provide the translation. Don't you think it is strange for the normal proceedings? I have never come across these kind of things, at least in my jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, Your Honour, I have just respectfully explained that I had given it for translation and that the Registry gave me an answer to the effect of what had actually happened. And that is precisely what I wished to do, in line with your ruling. I have the maximum and deepest respect for each and every one of your rulings. But as you can see, time has proven to be quite a difficulty. Your Honours, the "Islamic Declaration" is a very important issue because it is fundamental for the SDA programme. I'm not going to put questions about that now, but I shall certainly tender it later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And another thing is that if you need that translation from the Prosecutor's side, you have to do it outside the courtroom, rather than during the proceedings. We cannot spend so much time discussing about all those translations, and who will provide these translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm very embarrassed. I found this piece of information in my locker only 10 minutes ago. I have it here, the note that I found in my locker. It's the note that came from the Registry. I do apologise. I found this note only 10 minutes ago when I was coming back from the break, that the gentlemen from the OTP have a translation of it. I have the note here, handwritten. Well, very well. We'll move on to a completely different subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, can I ask you a question in relation to the cross-examining of this witness. Is it your case that because of certain documents that were published by one side or the other, that this was a reason why 20 mosques in the Mostar area should have been almost razed to the ground? If you feel this aspect of the case is extremely relevant, can't you call an expert witness? But at the moment, the value of this witness's evidence is that he personally saw, examined, and is aware of the systematic destruction of places of worship in the area where he is the Mufti. Now, are we ever going to get to the point where you're going to deal with that aspect of this witness's evidence? Is it in dispute that these 20 mosques were razed to the ground on direct orders and following a plan?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. Thank you for your suggestion. I will deal with this, and that is precisely where I wish to go, and that is why I am preparing a kind of background through my questions, because this is the finale, so to speak. I am doing this for the sake of the Trial Chamber, not for my own sake. If I'm not doing this well, I'm so sorry. I precisely want to paint a picture for you and to paint this picture through my questions, just like the direct examination showed various things relying on the Geneva conventions, but then we also want to prove things that are truthful and we want to prove them from the point of view of the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Krsnik, there's no charge in the indictment that anybody failed to adhere to the heads of agreement in the Geneva Convention. The problems that you have to deal with are the accusations that are made specifically against your clients, and as I understand it, the accusations that this witness is making, or that he's assisting the Prosecution in making, is that all the Muslim places of worship in the Mostar region were destroyed. And you know full well what the Geneva Convention and the rules of warfare say about that: deliberately destroyed. So you must address that. In due course, of course, you can call a witness to give background. We appreciate that there are two sides. But specifically, you must deal with the accusations that have been made against Mr. Naletilic. I'm sorry if I keep labouring this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. And I shall certainly bear this in mind. Actually, I am bearing this in mind. But in order to paint a broader picture, and in order to understand what preceded certain events - because nothing happens by accident - and once we get to the mosques, then you will hear my questions, because it's not such a simple question as it was put during the examination-in-chief. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Honourable witness, do you know Hafiz Halil efendi Meftic?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know Hasan Makic, who is a professor?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to tell this Trial Chamber what the Meshihat of the Islamic Community of Bosnia-Herzegovina is?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the supreme authority in the Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the Meshihat of the Islamic Community issued some instructions that are called "Instructions for Muslim Combatants" and every Muslim combatant had them in his pocket?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, this book was created in Zenica. I don't know if every soldier carried it. It depended on each and every soldier's own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, we got this translation on time. All of it is here. There are enough copies for all. So I would kindly ask the usher to have this distributed to all the parties, please. And for the gentleman, for our distinguished witness, we have a copy in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This exhibit is D1/25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've only been handed this exhibit, so of course, I can't completely know admittedly, but it seems that we are about to get into an area that implicates the submission that the Prosecution made a week or so ago in terms of such things what is called tu quoque and other issues in -- actually, we would say non-issues, in the case.
