Assuming for the moment that this document is what Mr. Krsnik says it is and assuming it says something about Muslim soldiers committing war crimes - I'm just simply making a fast characterisation - assuming all that's true, how is it relevant to this case and how is it relevant to an acceptable defence in the case? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I believe the jurisprudence of the Tribunal, coming from such cases as Kupreskic, is that if such evidence will be tendered to the Chamber, the Defence has to make a particularised showing as to how it is relevant to the case. That is what the Kupreskic Chamber ruled. I think other chambers have made similar rulings. And we object without that showing being made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Scott, these documents have just been distributed. You haven't heard the questions raised by Mr. Krsnik, so all your objection is based on the speculations. So let me hear the questions first. Then you will have full opportunity to object to what he's asking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And for your information, unfortunately, I'm sitting on the Kupreskic Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. You're absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Does this booklet contain instructions as to how the soldiers of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina are supposed to behave?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to read the book, and then I could answer you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I agree. I have quite a few questions, so perhaps I can leave you this copy. I am going to ask for a tape to be played now, D1/25. This is a 20-minute-long tape. So we won't be able to finish the cross-examination today. So I'll leave you that copy of the book, and then we shall continue discussing it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the permission of the Trial Chamber, one has to be familiar with the subject matter as a whole. Just as the honourable Presiding Judge said a few minutes ago, you took something out of context, and you left out the central issue, where it is said that Muslims are not in favour of divisions, but then with the second section, you were trying to prove that we were in favour of territorial divisions so again you can take a certain portion of the text out of context. I read this a long time ago, and I need to refresh my memory of this. These are general instructions that are valid for soldiers anywhere, because this is an Islamic moral pattern, so to speak. And in response to the question that you put to me, for a soldier of the army of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, you cannot say that this was for all of them. It is for individuals who wish their life to be governed by Islamic norms.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your answer. And now I would kindly ask the Trial Chamber to allow me to play a videotape. I think that the provisional number is D1/25 or 26, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, is there any protective measures concerning with this tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see any protective measures. However, there is a brief explanation involved. We tried for two days and we finally managed to make copies for the Prosecutor and for the Registrar, and we made abridged copies as well. So perhaps I could kindly ask the video director to fast-forward the beginning of the tape. It contains -- this tape contains a lineup of the entire 4th Corps that we have been discussing for such a long time now, so you will see that and you will hear my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll watch this --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is there audio to this tape, and has a transcript been prepared in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I haven't seen this tape yet and where it comes from. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is a comment, but I would just like certain persons who are on this tape to be identified. An English translation is underway, and I am going to be using this tape more from now on. In this particular case, I just wish certain persons to be identified. As for the authenticity of this tape, I am going to prove that with a witness who will testify within the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me say I am truly sorry to be on my feet so often this afternoon. I do not do it lightly, but I do believe there are serious issues. On this tape, if there is no transcript of what is said, then if the tape is going to be played now -- excuse me, I'll wait for Judge Clark. Excuse me, I was just waiting for Judge Clark. Sorry. If the tape is going to be played today, and if there is audio and if there is no translation of it, then I would -- at the most that only the video portion be played and not the audio portion, since we are completely unable to follow and understand what's happening. And I also just have a second question for counsel just for foundation. Could we have the location and date when this tape was made. We know nothing about the tape as it currently stands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have not seen this tape yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have seen it, Your Honour, to be perfectly honest. In fairness to counsel, it was given to us yesterday afternoon. But again, it's very poor quality, and there is no translation that has been provided. I can suggest to the Chamber, from what I have been told, it is something that happened in February 1995. But if we're not going to have a translation, Your Honour, we object to having the audio portion until there's a translation available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, would you please answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very gladly, Mr. President. Because it is quite clear to me why the Prosecutor is objecting to the audio version, and you will find it quite clear when you see the tape yourself, because as for the audio part, you don't really need a translation. Secondly, I'm saying this again. Again, we are having these debates in front of a witness. And the witness is on this tape. And he is saying something, and there are also some other questions that I cannot put in advance, so to speak. First we have to play the tape and then.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters' note is that without a transcript, they cannot give a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The authority of a religious leader and whether it exists and whether it doesn't exist is something that is shown on this tape, and the witness said that he attended many celebrations, and this is precisely what is shown here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We object strongly to this procedure. The reason that I am in the unfortunate position of having to be on my feet so often this afternoon is because counsel has repeatedly not followed this Chamber's directions. This Chamber has now, at least on three occasions, told them what the instructions are and has asked them to follow those instructions. We have now this afternoon been provided with two documents which Mr. Krsnik apparently feels are quite important. That's his right. But if they are that important, then the other side has to be able to read and have those same documents in front of them. Now he says that it has statements of the witness. Now those statements, we will not be able to follow. The simple reason that we are where we are is because counsel has not followed this Chamber's rulings. If all these translations had been provided, as this Chamber has ordered that they be provided, we would have done this an hour ago. We would have done it an hour ago. I do object. And I'm sorry, and I do apologise to the Chamber for being on my feet so much this afternoon. We object.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, please, this is the Arabic language. Nobody can translate that. Please, don't make me say everything in advance in front of the witness. Can this be called cross-examination, then? I mean, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, would you please tell us at least the sources of this tape, who made it, what it is about. Just give me a general idea of all this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was made by the press service of the 4th Corps. It's very clear. I explained this, that I made a shorter version, and now I'm going to play the longer version. And everything is on the cassette itself, who taped it, who made it, even the telephone number, if I'm not mistaken, where the tape could be ordered from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a parade of the ABiH in Jablanica in 1995. And when you see it, you will understand why I insist on it in the cross-examination, because very important questions flow out of that video cassette, and they concern this witness personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, after consultations among this Chamber, you are allowed to show this tape to us but without the audio part of this tape. We just want to see the images.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, please, the audio is essential here, because it proves that the ABiH was an army of a single ethnic group, of a single religion, and I am trying to impeach this witness here because the audio and the words spoken here are in the Arabic language. If necessary, I will spend the rest of the afternoon looking for an interpreter and I can provide the translation tomorrow. The interpreters, otherwise, could interpret this tape. Everything is very slow. But this is the first opportunity to see what types of armies the ABiH and HVO were. This is a crucial matter. This is why we are here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, let us watch this tape first without the audio part. If you think it's necessary for you to have the interpreters tomorrow, we could do it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. [Interpretation] Very well. Can I ask the technical group to please play it from the top.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video booth needs to know whether the tape is cued or not. In other words, is it ready to be played at the spot where you want it to start?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the top, yes. Yes, it could be rewound from the beginning. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I can be of assistance to the Trial Chamber, this -- the caption is, "The day of the 4th Motorised Light Brigade," and then underneath, it says that it is the press service of the 4th Jablanica Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we pause here, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recognise this person?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who it is?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the commander of the 4th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you pause here? If we can just go back a little bit? There.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, do you recognise this flag?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the parade --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm asking you about the flag. Do you recognise the flag?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not a member of the unit, so I cannot tell you, but it has some religious symbols there, even though I can't read -- I can't read the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The cameraman's name has now appeared on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you pause here, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Are you among these religious dignitaries?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see any religious dignitaries apart from myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see and I can't make out anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please pause here? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you now see the religious dignitaries?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see, but I can't make out their faces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll try later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that the outside monitors are projecting an image that is five times better. I don't know why we have such a poor quality of image in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please pause here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please tell us the name of this gentleman and what was his exact position in the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the commander of the 4th Muslim Brigade, Mr. Nezim Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that is part of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The brigade was part of the 4th Corps. [Videotape played].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you pause here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you tell the Trial Chamber who it is?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hamo Maslisa [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he represent the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a lawyer by profession. He was in various positions. I believe that he's a member of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can move on. Thank you to the technical booth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, is this you in the video?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell us today what you spoke about? Was this a speech of a religious leader or a military leader? -- if you recall. If not, doesn't matter.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no idea. But I was not a military leader, combat leader. I was a religious officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you pause here, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you recognise this man?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who it is.

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is Mahmut Karalic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was his position?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is from Zenica, from a Muslim unit there. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Was he not an emir?

utterances.speaker: SEID SMAJKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just by one clarification, on the transcript, the witness a moment ago was interpreted he was a religious officer. I just would appreciate some translation guidance. Did he say "religious officer" or "religious official"? Maybe the witness could also clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. Could you tell us whether it is "officer" or "official."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a dignitary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm asking the question to the witness himself, what he said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman said "commander" or some military commander of some kind, and I said, "No, I was not military. I didn't have a rank, and I did not have any position." So I was an officer of faith or a religious official or a dignitary, as the gentleman put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is about ten minutes left, Your Honours, and we will have a full translation tomorrow. So maybe tomorrow we can play the full tape complete with the video, but we will provide the video for tomorrow -- a transcript of the audio tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. We recognise that this tape was shot in 1995. How is it related to the incidents that happened in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in 1995, when the peace was reached, there were calls for the jihad. Tomorrow when you see the translation, you will see a connection between 1993 and 1995. You will see what things were like in 1995 in relation to 1993. That is the same corps that we have been dealing with throughout this case, which was created in late 1992, and because it had to be transferred to Jablanica because the Washington Accords stipulated that there be no military presence in Mostar, they were transferred to -- relocated to Jablanica. And with the other evidence that we will provide later on, we will counter the allegations by the Prosecution. Of course, this is not complete now because my learned friend was successful with his objection, but we will make a superhuman effort to provide a full transcript by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, on another matter, does this tape have a number? Because as I understand that, instructions to the Muslim fighters, this document, was numbered D1/25. So I wonder whether this tape has got a number. Maybe Madam Registrar could clear it up for me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd given it a number previously. It's D1/26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 4.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
